questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the roadway, what should you do?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely leave the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait until that vehicle has safely passed, then you may go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The highest safe speed when road and weather conditions are good.
The highest safe speed in all road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed when road and weather conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit depending on conditions. When conditions are poor, slow down.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to safely merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Let traffic on the freeway go first.

questions.explanation: Speed up on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic. Let traffic already on the freeway go first. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have enough space.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Let drivers already on the public road go first.
Expect other drivers to move out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers already on the public road go first.
questions.explanation: When you enter a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to traffic already on the public road. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up as they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver is behind you, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up or block them, as this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left turns are prohibited at this location.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and let pass:
questions.explanation: Before entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should cross. They may be marked with lines in any direction. Always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and carpools.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal in the direction you want to move. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol at a social event, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid driving while impaired is to arrange a ride with a friend who does not drink. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: You should not pass:

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, or on bridges. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: Passing is not allowed:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more space between your vehicle and the car ahead.
Be cautious around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snow and sleet, keep your windshield and mirrors clean. Leave extra space between your vehicle and others because slippery roads increase your stopping distance.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Always slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, around pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: Alcohol affects:
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol harm your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it means no parking in the fire zone.
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A red curb means you cannot park there because it is a fire zone.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk and pass on the left side.
Continue when you think children have finished exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm out. Do not move until the arm is pulled back.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger signals you to stop, when a stop sign is present, or when flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
How fast to drive in heavy traffic
How fast to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest or slowest speed allowed on that road. The maximum speed is for good conditions. You must slow down when weather or traffic is bad.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What is the best way to protect yourself from injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level?

options.text: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. They may keep you alert, but they cannot make you sober or change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Which word describes a defensive driver?
questions.explanation: Good defensive drivers have the skills to drive safely through traffic without endangering others. They watch for blind spots, look ahead, stay focused, and follow road rules.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Make sure the new lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Turn your head to check your blind spot. Make sure the new lane is clear before moving.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no cars are coming.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Stop like you would at a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop like you would at a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn of dangerous intersections. Treat them as stop signs.

questions.question: What should you do if a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light?

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic signals.

questions.question: Which substances can make you unsafe to drive and get you arrested for DUII?
questions.explanation: Many substances can make you unsafe to drive. These include all types of alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many medicines (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tire tread in good condition.
Keep your tires filled to the correct pressure.
Slow down when it is raining.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, maintain good tire tread and proper tire pressure. Slow down in the rain because hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.
